newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes recover slightly on buying late.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes recover slightly on buying late.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices recovered slightly late Tuesday as some refiners stepped up April buying, traders said.
But the market is likely to remain sloppy until some of the excess supply is soaked up, traders said.
Weekly American Petroleum Institute (API) data, due out tonight, is widely expected to indicate a hefty crude stock build of around 3.5 million barrels, traders said.
April West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was trading around $20.10-20 a barrel late afternoon, down 30 cents from late Monday's cash market.
West Texas Intermediate/Midland last traded at WTI/Cushing minus 37 cents a barrel, two cents stronger from Monday's highest trade.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was at minus 32-25 cents, with the last trade at minus 25 cents versus 30 and 35 cents earlier in the day.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire was at minus 55-45 cents, with deals between minus 50 and minus 58 cents, compared to minus 60 cents on Monday.
West Texas Sour/Midland was around minus 2.70-2.65 a barrel. The day's highest trades were minus $2.68 and possibly minus $2.65, up from minus $2.72 on Monday.
Eugene Island last traded at minus $2.52, steady with Monday.
WTI/Cushing Posting Plus was at $1.54-56 a barrel, reflecting the recently achieved contango between April/May and May/June WTI.
